newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arab-Israeli scuffles erupt near settlement site.
newsitem.headline: Arab-Israeli scuffles erupt near settlement site.

text.p: Israeli soldiers scuffled with Arabs near a planned Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on Tuesday minutes after bulldozers broke ground on the housing project, witnesses said.
At least three Israeli Arab students from Jerusalem's Hebrew University were hurt trying to reach a Palestinian protest camp when the soldiers hit them with rifle butts, the witnesses said.
"It is a black day in the history of the peace process," Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat told reporters in the self-ruled Gaza Strip.
Israel stationed soldiers around Jabal Ghneim, a pine-covered hilltop where it plans to build 6,500 homes for Jews. One of four bulldozers that arrived at the site began digging immediately.

PLO official Faisal al-Husseini, leading a tent-camp protest opposite the site Israel calls Har Homa, told reporters the groundbreaking had left Palestinians with only one option -- "to go down to the streets".
"I have long worked for peace and never despaired. But today I am beginning to despair that peace negotiations will be useful," Husseini said.

Husseini and Palestinian Legislative Council speaker Ahmed Korei, an architect of Israeli-PLO peace deals, tried to lead a group of about 30 Palestinians in a march from the encampment to the hill. But Israeli soldiers forced them to stop.
The Israeli army said that as a precautionary measure it had removed Jewish worshippers from Joseph's Tomb, a Jewish shrine and seminary in the Palestinian self-ruled town of Nablus in the West Bank.

But it said Israeli soldiers remained at the shrine, scene of a gun battle last September after Israel's opening of another entrance to an archaeological tunnel in East Jerusalem touched off violence that killed 61 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.
Palestinians see East Jerusalem -- which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war -- as the capital of a future state, but Israel says all of Jerusalem will forever be the Jewish state's capital.

Erekat said the Palestinian leadership -- composed of the cabinet of the Palestinian Authority and the Palestine Liberation Organisation's executive committee -- would hold an emergency meeting on Tuesday to discuss a response.
"We realise that this government will use the bulldozers in order to shut the door to negotiations and remove any meaning from the peace process," Erekat said.
"It (the leadership) will discuss the response by all means available. We will wait for the decision of the leadership," he said.
